## §2.1.1: The Quest for Universality & The Syntrix Triad {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-d">LEVEL II OF KONSTITUTIONSSTAMMBAUM &amp; STRATUM D (SM, PP. 24–27, EQ. 5)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="52%"}
### Overcoming the Generative Deficit of Sheaf Descent
* In Chapter 1 (Level I), the sheaf topos $\Esyn$ restricted and glued existing local observations into Holoforms $\mathsf{Hol}(\mathcal{U}, \mathbf{P})$. Yet a sheaf is **passive**: it cannot raise tensor ranks or synthesize higher-order concepts.
* In §2.1 (SM, pp. 24–27), Heim seeks a **Universalquantor ($\mathbf{U}$)**—an invariant law valid across *all* conceivable aspect systems. Concatenating aspect-variant functors ($\mathfrak{F}$) yields only regional Polyquantors ($Q_{\mathrm{poly}}$).
* Following **Ernst Cassirer (1910)** (*Substanzbegriff und Funktionsbegriff*), the operands of a Universalquantor must be complete, hierarchically generated conceptual systems—**Kategorien ($\mathfrak{K}$)**—unfolded by the **Syntrix ($\syntrix$)**.

::: {.thm-box .fragment}
**The Syntrix Triad (SM, p. 27, Eq. 5):**
$$
\syntrix \equiv \langle \synkolator,\, \metrophor,\, m \rangle \quad \lor \quad \metrophor \equiv (a_i)_n \quad \lor \quad F_1 \equiv \synkolator(a_k)_1^m \quad \lor \quad 1 \le m \le n \tag{SM-5}
$$

1. **The Metrophor ($\metrophor \equiv (a_i)_n$):** Invariant apodictic base $\AP_0$ (*Idee* $\mathfrak{S}_1$, *Maßträger*).
2. **The Synkolator ($\synkolator$):** *Syndromkorrelationsstufeninduktor* driving upward synthesis ($F_\gamma \to F_{\gamma+1}$, **Episyllogismus** $k \uparrow$).
3. **The Synkolationsstufe ($m \in \mathbb{N}$):** Operational arity binding $m$ inputs per generative step.
:::

:::

::: {.column width="48%"}

<div class="video-container">
  <video autoplay data-autoplay loop muted playsinline src="media/Ch2_Act1_Syntrix_Triad.mp4" style="max-height:330px;"></video>
  <div class="video-caption">Manim Act I: Cassirer's Substance-to-Function Shift &amp; The Syntrix Triad (SM-5)</div>
</div>

::: {.intuition-box .fragment}
**Recursive Unfolding of the Syndrome Tower:**
$$
\metrophor = F_0 \xrightarrow{\;\synkolator_1\;} F_1 \xrightarrow{\;\synkolator_2\;} F_2 \xrightarrow{\;\synkolator_3\;} \cdots \xrightarrow{\;\synkolator_\gamma\;} F_\gamma
$$
Every derived concept traces its semantic stability back to the unconditioned Metrophor $\metrophor$.
:::

:::

::::

::: {.notes}
Welcome to Chapter 2, which ascends to Level II of the Syntrometric Konstitutionsstammbaum: Quasi-Analytic Concept Generation. While Chapter 1 showed how local observer perspectives glue via sheaf descent, a sheaf cannot synthesize higher-order concepts. Heim's Syntrix triad (SM Eq. 5) acts as a functorial operand that unfolds an ascending tower of syndromes F_1, F_2, ..., F_gamma from an invariant apodictic base—the Metrophor.
:::

## §2.1.2–2.1.4: Pyramidal vs. Homogeneous & *Bandsyntrix* {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-d">STRATUM D: SPALTBARKEIT (SM-5a), EXISTENZBEDINGUNG (SM-6) &amp; BANDSYNTRIX (SM-7)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}
### Two Dependency Architectures (SM, pp. 28–29)
* **Pyramidal Syntrix ($y\syntrix$ — *Diskrete Synkolation*):** Strict level-by-level progression where $F_{\gamma+1}$ draws its $m$ inputs exclusively from $F_\gamma$.
* **Homogeneous Syntrix ($\homsyntrix$ — *Kontinuierliche Synkolation*):** Cumulative historical memory drawing inputs simultaneously from $\metrophor$ and all preceding layers $(F_1, \dots, F_\gamma)$:
$$
\homsyntrix \equiv \langle\langle \synkolator,\, \metrophor \rangle m \rangle \tag{SM-5a}
$$

::: {.carnap-box .fragment}
***Spaltbarkeit*, *Existenzbedingung* (SM-6) & *Bandsyntrix* (SM-7):**

1. **Spaltbarkeit (SM, p. 29):** Every homogeneous Syntrix factors into a pyramidal core ($T_{\mathrm{pyr}}$) and a residual interaction fragment ($T_{\mathrm{frag}}$, *Homogenfragment*).
2. **Existenzbedingung (SM-6) & Bandsyntrix (SM-7):**
$$
\metrophor \equiv (a_i)_n \;\;(n \ge 1), \qquad \metrophor_{\mathrm{band}} \equiv (A_i,\, a_i,\, B_i)_n \tag{SM-6, SM-7}
$$
**Prop. 2.1 & Thm. 2.2:** Discrete syntrices are the degenerate interval case $A_i = B_i = a_i$ ($\Delta_i = 0$).
:::

:::

## §2.2.1–2.2.2: The $\mathsf{Ban}$-Enriched Colored Operad $\Osyn$ {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM A: COMPLETED COLORED BANACH OPERADS (DEFS. 2.3–2.5, FIG. 2.1)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.intuition-box}
**Why Colored Operads Govern the Syntrix:**
Each hierarchical level $\gamma \in \Col \coloneqq \mathbb{N}_0$ acts as an unforgeable type tag ("color"). An operation $f \in \Osyn(\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_m; \gamma)$ can fire if and only if its input slots match the exact structural grades of the incoming syndromes.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment}
**Definition 2.4: Completed Free Operad $\widehat{\mathbb{F}}_\pi(E)$ via Colored Trees**
Let $E_{\mathrm{pyr}}(\gamma,\dots,\gamma; \gamma+1)$ denote single-step uniform operations and $E_{\mathrm{hom}}(\vec{\gamma}; \gamma+1)$ ($\max \gamma_i \le \gamma$) denote historical operations. For each rooted tree $\tau \in \operatorname{Tree}(\vec{\gamma}; \gamma)$:
$$
E(\tau) \coloneqq \widehat{\bigotimes}_{v \in V(\tau)}^\pi E(\operatorname{in}(v); \operatorname{out}(v)), \qquad \widehat{\mathbb{F}}_\pi(E)(\vec{\gamma}; \gamma) \coloneqq \bigoplus_{[\tau] \in \operatorname{Tree}(\vec{\gamma}; \gamma)/\sim}^{\ell^1} E(\tau)_{\Aut(\tau)}
$$
where $E(\tau)_{\Aut(\tau)} = E(\tau) / \overline{\operatorname{span}}\{u - \sigma \cdot u\}$, subject to **Substitution Contraction** ($\|\circ_i\|_{\op} \le 1$) and **Strict Unit Isometry** ($\|\operatorname{id}_c\|_{\Osyn(c;c)} = 1$).
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment}
**Definition 2.5: Syntrix Algebras over $\Osyn$**
An $\Osyn$-algebra on graded Banach spaces $F = \{F_\gamma\}_{\gamma \ge 0}$ is an operad morphism $A \colon \Osyn \to \operatorname{End}(F)$ with contractive evaluations:
$$
\operatorname{ev}_{\vec{\gamma}; \gamma} \colon \Osyn(\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_m; \gamma) \otpi \big(F_{\gamma_1} \otpi \dots \otpi F_{\gamma_m}\big) \longrightarrow F_\gamma
$$
:::

:::

## §2.2.3: Operational Stabilizers $\Stab(f)$ & Permutohedron $\Pi_3$ {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM A: SYMMETRY ORBITS &amp; LAGRANGE INDEX (DEF. 2.6, FIG. 2.2)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="46%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Definition 2.6: Profile-Preserving Stabilizers & Asymmetry Index**
For colored profile $\vec{\gamma} = (\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_m)$, let $\Sigma_{\vec{\gamma}} \coloneqq \{\sigma \in \Sigma_m \mid \gamma_{\sigma^{-1}(i)} = \gamma_i\}$.

1. **Operational Stabilizer Subgroup:**
$$
\Stab(f) \;\coloneqq\; \{ \sigma \in \Sigma_{\vec{\gamma}} \mid \sigma \cdot f = f \}
$$
2. **Permutation Asymmetry Measure (Lagrange Orbit Index):**
$$
r_f \;\coloneqq\; [\Sigma_{\vec{\gamma}} : \Stab(f)] \;=\; \frac{|\Sigma_{\vec{\gamma}}|}{|\Stab(f)|}
$$
* **Fully Symmetric Operation:** $\Stab(f) = \Sigma_{\vec{\gamma}} \iff r_f = 1$.
* **Partially Asymmetric (Fig. 2.2):** $\Stab(f) = \langle s_1 \rangle \subset \Sigma_3 \iff r_f = 6/2 = 3$ cosets.
* **Completely Asymmetric:** $\Stab(f) = \{e\} \iff r_f = m!$.
:::

## §2.2.4–2.2.5: Free Tree Monad $T_{\mathsf{P}}$ & Bar–Cobar Duality {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM A: EPISYLLOGISMUS MONAD (DEF. 2.7) &amp; PROSYLLOGISMUS COOPERAD (DEF. 2.8, THM. 2.9)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Definition 2.7: Completed Free Tree Monad $T_{\mathsf{P}}$ (*Episyllogismus* $k \uparrow$)**
For bounded polynomial functor $\mathsf{P}(Y) \coloneqq \bigoplus_{m=1}^M (E(m) \otpi Y^{\otpi m})_{\Sigma_m}$ on $\Ban$, the $\ell^1$-completed initial algebra of $\mathsf{F}_X(Y) = X \oplus_1 \mathsf{P}(Y)$ is:
$$
T_{\mathsf{P}}(X) \;\cong\; X \oplus_1 \mathsf{P}(T_{\mathsf{P}}(X)) \;\cong\; \bigoplus_{[\tau] \in \mathbf{Tree}/\sim}^{\ell^1} \left( E(\tau) \otpi X^{\otpi \operatorname{Leaves}(\tau)} \right)_{\Aut(\tau)}
$$
Under finite tree-depth bound $K \in \mathbb{N}$ (or heterometral *Syndromabschluß*), $T_{\mathsf{P}}^{(\le K)}$ restricts to $\FinBan \to \FinBan$ (**Claim Ceiling $c_{\mathrm{MONAD}}$**).
:::

::: {.carnap-box .fragment}
**Definition 2.8 & Theorem 2.9: Bar–Cobar Duality (*Prosyllogismus* $k \downarrow$)**
The downward analytical decomposition of syndromes is governed by the **Prosyllogistic Bar Cooperad** $B(\Osyn) \coloneqq \mathbb{F}^c(s\overline{\Osyn})$ (acting by **tree de-grafting** $\Delta_{\mathrm{prosyl}}$):
$$
\Omega_{\mathrm{cobar}} \;\dashv\; B_{\mathrm{bar}} \;\colon\; \mathbf{dgOp}_{\Col}^{\mathrm{aug}} \;\rightleftarrows\; \mathbf{dgCoop}_{\Col}^{\mathrm{conil}}
$$
The counit $\epsilon_{\mathcal{O}} \colon \Omega_{\mathrm{cobar}}(B_{\mathrm{bar}}(\Osyn)) \xrightarrow{\sim} \Osyn$ is a quasi-isomorphism!
:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

<div class="video-container">
  <video autoplay data-autoplay loop muted playsinline src="media/Ch2_Act5_Tree_Monad_Bar_Cobar.mp4" style="max-height:280px;"></video>
  <div class="video-caption">Manim Act V: Iterative Tree Monad T_P(X) (k ↑) vs. Prosyllogistic Bar Cooperad De-Grafting (k ↓)</div>
</div>

::: {.intuition-box .fragment}
**Prosyllogistic Comodulization & Twisting Cochains (§2.2.5):**
$$
\delta_{k\downarrow} \colon F_\gamma \longrightarrow \bigoplus_{\vec{\gamma} \in \Col^m} B(\Osyn)(\vec{\gamma}; \gamma) \otpi \big(F_{\gamma_1} \otpi \dots \otpi F_{\gamma_m}\big)
$$
Morphisms $\Omega_{\mathrm{cobar}}(\mathcal{C}) \to \mathcal{O}$ correspond bijectively to twisting morphisms $\alpha \in \operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ satisfying the Maurer–Cartan equation $\partial(\alpha) + \alpha \star \alpha = 0$.
:::

:::

::::

::: {.notes}
While the free tree monad T_P formalizes the upward constructive Episyllogismus (grafting trees from the Metrophor), modern operad theory provides the exact dual machine for Heim's downward analytical Prosyllogismus: the Operadic Bar Construction B(O_syn), which decomposes a composite syndrome into its ancestral lineage via tree de-grafting.
:::

## §2.3–2.4.1: Leveled Category $\CSL$, Spine & 4 Elementary Structures {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: SHIFT ENDOFUNCTOR (PROP. 2.13) &amp; SELECTION REPRESENTATIONS (THMS. 2.17–2.22)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="47%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Definitions 2.10–2.16: $\CSL(\mathcal{B})$, $\Shift$ & Thin Spine $\Cspine$**
* Objects $\mathbf{L} = (P_k, S_k, (I_j^+)_{j\ge 1}, O_k)_{k\in\mathbb{N}_0}$ track propositions, stability $S_k$, ancestral parthood $I_k^+$, and Metrophor origin $O_k$ over $\mathfrak{f}_{\mathrm{ops}}(P) = \{\operatorname{Conj}, \operatorname{Lift}_{\BoxSyn}, \operatorname{ParaConj}\}$.
* The **Level-Shift Functor** $\Shift(\mathbf{L})_k \coloneqq \mathbf{L}_{k+1}$ generates the **thin spine subcategory** $\Cspine \cong (\mathbb{N}_0, \le)$ of shifted free levels $\mathbf{L}^{(k)} \coloneqq \Shift^k(\mathbf{L}^*)$ (Fig. 2.4).
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment}
**Theorem 2.17, Lemma 2.18 & Theorem 2.22: Selection Dimensions**
On an $n$-dimensional carrier $V \in \FinBan$ with arity $m$:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\dim \mathcal{S}_{(1)}\;(\Lambda^m V) &= \binom{n}{m}, & \dim \mathcal{S}_{(2)}\;(V^{\underline{\otimes}m}) &= \frac{n!}{(n-m)!} \\
\dim \mathcal{S}_{(3)}\;(\Sym^m V) &= \binom{n+m-1}{m}, & \dim \mathcal{S}_{(4)}\;(V^{\otimes m}) &= n^m
\end{aligned}
$$
* **Lemma 2.18 ($k$-Fold Asymmetric Bridge):** $n_1 = k!\binom{m}{k}\binom{n}{m} = \frac{n!}{(m-k)!(n-m)!}$.
* **Thm 2.22 (Homometral Class):** $A \coloneqq m - \sum_{j=1}^L (a_j - 1) \implies n_{\gamma+1} = \binom{n_\gamma}{A}$.
:::

## §2.4.2–2.4.3: *Komplexsynkolatoren* & Dynamical Phase Trichotomy {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: PROGRAMMABLE CLOSURE (PROP. 2.25) &amp; PHASE TRICHOTOMY (THM. 2.26, FIG. 2.6)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="47%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Def. 2.24 & Prop. 2.25: *Komplexsynkolatoren* & *Syndromabschluß* (SM-8)**
Stepping arity $m(\gamma) = \sum_{k=1}^K m_k \mathbf{1}_{I_k}(\gamma)$ across interval partitions $I_k = [\chi(k-1), \chi(k)-1]$ ($\chi!$ execution orderings, **Thm. 2.20**):
$$
m_K > \dim\big(F_{\chi(K-1)}\big) \implies \dim \Lambda^{m_K}\big(F_{\chi(K-1)}\big) = \binom{\dim F}{m_K} = 0
$$
forcing deterministic **Syndromabschluß**: $F_\gamma \cong \{0\}$ for all $\gamma \ge \chi(K)$.
:::

::: {.carnap-box .fragment}
**Theorem 2.26: Dynamical Phase Trichotomy of $n_{\gamma+1} = \binom{n_\gamma}{m}$**

1. **Sub-Critical Extinction ($n_0 \le m$ — *Syndromabschluß*):** Terminates in $\le 2$ steps ($n_\gamma = 0\;\forall \gamma \ge 2$).
2. **Critical Equi-Syndromatic Fixed Point ($n_0 = m + 1$ — *Äquisyndromatik*):** Strictly constant $n_\gamma = m + 1\;\forall \gamma \ge 0$ (Lean 4: `equisyndromatic_fixed_point`).
3. **Super-Critical Doubly-Exponential ($n_0 \ge m + 2$):**
$$
\lim_{\gamma \to \infty} \frac{1}{m^\gamma} \ln n_\gamma = \theta(n_0, m) > 0, \qquad n_\gamma \sim (m!)^{\frac{1}{m-1}} \exp\!\big(\theta(n_0, m)\, m^\gamma\big)
$$
:::

:::

## §2.5: Boardman–Vogt Tensor & Beck Distributive Law {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: OPERADIC SPALTBARKEIT (DEF. 2.28) &amp; BECK COHERENCE (THM. 2.29, FIGS. 2.3 &amp; 2.7)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="46%"}

::: {.firewall-box}
**Why Naive Free-Tree Substitution Fails I**
On raw unquotiented syntax trees $\mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}, \mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{frag}}$, pushing a multi-ary pyramidal node across a fragment node duplicates subtrees, violating Beck's multiplication pentagon (Plotkin 2004; Klin 2013).
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment}
**Def. 2.28 & Thm. 2.29: Boardman–Vogt Quotient & Beck Law**
Quotienting by the multilinear interchange ideal $\mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{exchange}}$:
$$
\Ohom \;\coloneqq\; \Opyr \otBV \Ofrag \;\coloneqq\; \frac{\Opyr \amalg \Ofrag}{\langle f \circ (g,\dots,g) \sim \sigma_{n,m}\cdot g \circ (f,\dots,f) \rangle}
$$
induces a contractive **Beck Distributive Law** on the $\ell^1$-completed quotient monads:
$$
\widehat{\lambda}_X \colon \overline{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}\big(\overline{T}_{\mathrm{frag}} X\big) \longrightarrow \overline{T}_{\mathrm{frag}}\big(\overline{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}} X\big), \qquad \|\widehat{\lambda}_X\|_{\op} \le 1
$$
yielding the composite monad $T_{\mathrm{hom}} \coloneqq \overline{T}_{\mathrm{frag}} \circ \overline{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}$ whose algebras coincide with $\operatorname{Alg}_{\Ohom}(\Ban)$.
:::

<div class="video-container" style="margin-top:8px;">

  <div class="video-caption">Manim Acts IX &amp; X (Figs. 2.3 &amp; 2.7): Syntrix Crystal Lattice &amp; Beck Coherence Diagrams</div>
</div>

:::

::: {#beck-pane-1 .syn-tab-pane .active}
**1. Operadic *Spaltbarkeit* via Boardman–Vogt Tensor Product (Def. 2.28)**
$$
f \circ (g, \dots, g) \;\sim\; \sigma_{n,m} \cdot \big( g \circ (f, \dots, f) \big) \quad \pmod{\mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{exchange}}}
$$
By universal property, an $\Ohom$-algebra is canonically an $\Opyr$-algebra internal to $\operatorname{Alg}_{\Ofrag}(\Ban)$:
$$
\operatorname{Alg}_{\Ohom}(\Ban) \;\cong\; \operatorname{Alg}_{\Opyr}\!\Big( \operatorname{Alg}_{\Ofrag}(\Ban) \Big)
$$
:::

::: {#beck-pane-2 .syn-tab-pane}
**2. Recursive Presentation of the Interchange Transformation $\lambda_X$ (Prop. 2.30)**
* **Unit Base Case:** $\lambda_X(\eta_{\mathrm{pyr}}(u)) = \overline{T}_{\mathrm{frag}}(\eta_{\mathrm{pyr}} X)(u)$ for all $u \in \overline{T}_{\mathrm{frag}} X$.
* **Interchange Distribution:** For $\psi \in \Opyr(n)$ and $u_1, \dots, u_n \in \overline{T}_{\mathrm{frag}} X$:
$$
\lambda_X\big(\psi(u_1, \dots, u_n)\big) \;=\; \Big[ \mu_{\mathrm{frag}} \circ \overline{T}_{\mathrm{frag}}(\psi)\big(\lambda_X(u_1), \dots, \lambda_X(u_n)\big) \Big]_{\mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{exchange}}}
$$
Pulls historical cross-level interactions ($\overline{T}_{\mathrm{frag}}$) to the outer layer while keeping step-by-step deduction ($\overline{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}$) in the inner core!
:::

::: {#beck-pane-3 .syn-tab-pane}
**3. Beck Multiplication Pentagon & Composite Multiplication $\mu_{\mathrm{hom}}$ (Fig. 2.7A)**
$$
\mu_{\mathrm{hom}} \;\coloneqq\; (\mu_{\mathrm{frag}} \overline{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}) \circ (\overline{T}_{\mathrm{frag}} \overline{T}_{\mathrm{frag}} \mu_{\mathrm{pyr}}) \circ (\overline{T}_{\mathrm{frag}} \widehat{\lambda} \overline{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}})
$$
Satisfies the two Beck multiplication pentagons (`mult_pyr` and `mult_frag` in `Syntrometrie.StratumA.Operads.BeckDistributiveLaw`):
$$
(\mu_{\mathrm{pyr}} \overline{T}_{\mathrm{frag}}) \Rightarrow \widehat{\lambda} \;=\; (\overline{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}\widehat{\lambda}) \Rightarrow (\widehat{\lambda}\overline{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}) \Rightarrow (\overline{T}_{\mathrm{frag}}\mu_{\mathrm{pyr}})
$$
:::

::: {#beck-pane-4 .syn-tab-pane}
**4. Beck Unit Triangles & Composite Unit $\eta_{\mathrm{hom}}$ (Fig. 2.7B)**
$$
\eta_{\mathrm{hom}} \;\coloneqq\; (\eta_{\mathrm{frag}} \overline{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}) \circ \eta_{\mathrm{pyr}} \colon \operatorname{Id}_{\Ban} \Longrightarrow \overline{T}_{\mathrm{frag}} \circ \overline{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}
$$
Satisfies both unit compatibility triangles (`unit_pyr` and `unit_frag`):
$$
\widehat{\lambda} \circ (\eta_{\mathrm{pyr}} \overline{T}_{\mathrm{frag}}) = \overline{T}_{\mathrm{frag}} \eta_{\mathrm{pyr}}, \qquad \widehat{\lambda} \circ (\overline{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}} \eta_{\mathrm{frag}}) = \eta_{\mathrm{frag}} \overline{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}
$$
:::

:::

:::

::::

::: {.notes}
Section 2.5 provides the exact algebraic proof of Heim's Spaltbarkeit. Because unrestricted free tree monads do not distribute over each other without duplicating subtrees, we quotient by the Boardman-Vogt interchange ideal I_exchange and extend continuously to the l^1-completions via the Bounded Linear Transformation (BLT) theorem, yielding a contractive Beck Distributive Law lambda_hat.
:::

::: {#stab-pane-1 .syn-tab-pane .active}
**1. Hereditary Semantics of $\BoxSyn \phi$ & Demarcation from $\Box_S \phi$ (Rem. 2.3)**
* **Base ($a_i \in P_0 = \AP_0$):** $(U, k) \models \BoxSyn a_i \iff a_i \in \AP_0 \wedge (U, k) \models a_i$.
* **Inductive ($\phi \in P_{p+1},\; p+1 \le k$):**
$$
(U, k) \models \BoxSyn \phi \;\Longleftrightarrow\; (U, k) \models \phi \;\wedge\; \forall X \in P_p\big((X, \phi) \in I_{p+1} \implies (U, k) \models \BoxSyn X\big)
$$
:::

::: {#stab-pane-2 .syn-tab-pane}
**2. Syntrix-Internal Stability Introduction Rules ($\BoxSyn\mathfrak{a}I, \BoxSyn FI$)**
$$
\frac{a_i \in \AP_0 \qquad S(x); \Gamma \vdash^0 a_i}{S(x); \Gamma \vdash^0 \BoxSyn a_i}\;(\BoxSyn\mathfrak{a}I)
$$
$$
\frac{S(x); \Gamma \vdash^{j+1} \phi' \qquad \forall X \in P_j\,\big((X, \phi') \in I_{j+1} \to S(x); \Gamma \vdash^j \BoxSyn X\big)}{S(x); \Gamma \vdash^{j+1} \BoxSyn \phi'}\;(\BoxSyn FI)
$$
:::

::: {#stab-pane-3 .syn-tab-pane}
**3. Syntrix-Internal Stability Elimination Rules ($\BoxSyn E_T, \BoxSyn E_{\mathrm{IGP}}$)**
$$
\frac{S(x); \Gamma \vdash^j \BoxSyn \phi}{S(x); \Gamma \vdash^j \phi}\;(\BoxSyn E_T) \qquad\qquad \frac{S(x); \Gamma \vdash^{j+1} \BoxSyn \phi' \qquad ((X, \phi') \in I_{j+1})}{S(x); \Gamma \vdash^j \BoxSyn X}\;(\BoxSyn E_{\mathrm{IGP}})
$$
:::

::: {#stab-pane-4 .syn-tab-pane}
**4. Spine Reflexivity Natural Transformation $\rho^{(n)} \colon \operatorname{Id}_{\Cspine} \Longrightarrow \Shift^n|_{\Cspine}$ (Thm. 2.33, Fig. 2.8)**
Componentwise $(\rho_k^{(n)})_j(X) \coloneqq \operatorname{Lift}_{\BoxSyn}^n(X)$ commutes strictly with spine morphisms $f_k \colon \mathbf{L}^{(k)} \to \mathbf{L}^{(k+1)}$:
$$
\Shift^n(f_k) \circ \rho_k^{(n)} = \rho_{k+1}^{(n)} \circ f_k \;=\; \operatorname{Lift}_{\BoxSyn}^{n+1}, \qquad \rho_{k+n}^{(m)} \circ \rho_k^{(n)} = \rho_k^{(n+m)}
$$
:::

## §2.8: The *Äondyne* Fibration, Holonomy Circles & Quasi-Analysis {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM A/B: GROTHENDIECK FIBRATION (THM. 2.35), POLYCYCLIC CIRCLES &amp; QUASI-ANALYSIS (THM. 2.38)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Def. 2.34 & Thm. 2.35: The *Äondyne* Grothendieck Fibration (Fig. 2.9)**
A parameterized *Äondyne* over $U \in \Ctx$ is a tuple $\underline{\mathbf{S}} = (\metrophor, f, \vec{\gamma}, \gamma, \mathsf{Sel}_m)$ with $\metrophor \in C^0(M_U, (P^U)^n)$ and $f \in C^0(M'_U, \Osyn(\vec{\gamma}; \gamma))$. The Grothendieck construction:
$$
\pi \colon \int_{\Ctx} \mathbf{Syn} \longrightarrow \Ctx, \qquad (U, \underline{\mathbf{S}}) \longmapsto U
$$
is a **Grothendieck fibration** whose Cartesian lifts $h^*(\underline{\mathbf{S}})$ transport entire Syntrix hierarchies across context manifolds.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment}
**Def. 2.36 & Thm. 2.37: Boundary Topology & Dimension Convergence**
* **Boundary Forms:** Closed $[\alpha, \beta]$, Half-open / Radial (*Radialformen*) $[\alpha, \beta)$, Open $(\alpha, \beta)$.
* **Syndrome Dimension Limit:** For component parameter dimensions $n_i$ ($N \coloneqq \sum_i n_i$) and arity $m > 1$:
$$
\mu(\gamma) \ge n_i, \qquad \lim_{\gamma \to \infty} \mu(\gamma) = N = \sum_{i=1}^n n_i
$$
:::

::: {.carnap-box .fragment}
**Theorem 2.38 ($c_{\mathrm{QUASI}}$): Carnapian Quasi-Analysis via Tree Monads**
$$
\operatorname{QuasiAnalyse}(X) \;\coloneqq\; T_{\mathsf{P}}(X) \in \operatorname{Alg}_{\Osyn}(\Ban)
$$
Higher concepts are coinvariant trees of operadic relations, not reified substances (French 2014).
:::

<script>
window.comb2 = function(n, k) {
  if (k < 0 || k > n) return 0;
  if (k === 0 || k === n) return 1;
  let res = 1;
  for (let i = 1; i <= k; i++) {
    res = res * (n - i + 1) / i;
  }
  return Math.round(res);
};

window.fact2 = function(n) {
  let r = 1;
  for (let i = 2; i <= n; i++) r *= i;
  return r;
};

window.updateSelectionDims = function() {
  const elN = document.getElementById('sel-n');
  if (!elN) return;
  let n = parseInt(elN.value);
  let m = parseInt(document.getElementById('sel-m').value);
  let kInput = document.getElementById('sel-k');
  kInput.max = m;
  let k = Math.min(m, parseInt(kInput.value));
  kInput.value = k;

  let repInput = document.getElementById('sel-rep');
  repInput.max = Math.max(0, m - 1);
  let rep = Math.min(Math.max(0, m - 1), parseInt(repInput.value));
  repInput.value = rep;

  document.getElementById('sel-n-val').innerText = n;
  document.getElementById('sel-m-val').innerText = m;
  document.getElementById('sel-k-val').innerText = k;
  document.getElementById('sel-rep-val').innerText = rep;

  let s1 = window.comb2(n, m);
  let s2 = (m <= n) ? s1 * window.fact2(m) : 0;
  let s3 = window.comb2(n + m - 1, m);
  let s4 = Math.pow(n, m);

  let asymK = (m <= n) ? window.fact2(k) * window.comb2(m, k) * window.comb2(n, m) : 0;
  let effA = m - rep;
  let homPop = window.comb2(n, effA);

  document.getElementById('sel-bars').innerHTML = `
    <div class="stat-card" style="border-left-color:#4169E1;">
      <b style="color:#82aaff;">S₍₁₎ Het, Sym (Λ^m V):</b><br>C(${n}, ${m}) = <b style="color:#FFD700;">${s1.toLocaleString()}</b> ${s1===0 ? '<span style="color:#ff6b81;">(Closed!)</span>' : ''}
    </div>
    <div class="stat-card" style="border-left-color:#20B2AA;">
      <b style="color:#5eead4;">S₍₂₎ Het, Asym (V^{⊗_dist m}):</b><br>n!/(n-m)! = <b style="color:#FFD700;">${s2.toLocaleString()}</b>
    </div>
    <div class="stat-card" style="border-left-color:#FFA500;">
      <b style="color:#fcd34d;">S₍₃₎ Hom, Sym (Sym^m V):</b><br>C(${n+m-1}, ${m}) = <b style="color:#FFD700;">${s3.toLocaleString()}</b>
    </div>
    <div class="stat-card" style="border-left-color:#a855f7;">
      <b style="color:#e9d5ff;">S₍₄₎ Hom, Asym (V^{⊗m}):</b><br>${n}^${m} = <b style="color:#FFD700;">${s4.toLocaleString()}</b>
    </div>
  `;

  const brBox = document.getElementById('sel-bridge-readout');
  if (brBox) {
    brBox.innerText =
      `Lemma 2.18 (k=${k} Asymmetry): k!C(m,k)C(n,m) = ${asymK.toLocaleString()}  |  Thm 2.22 (Effective Class A = m - ∑(a_j-1) = ${effA}): C(${n}, ${effA}) = ${homPop.toLocaleString()}` +
      ((effA === 1 || m === n - 1) ? " [ÄQUISYNDROMATIK: n₁ = n!]" : "");
  }
};

window.setSelPreset = function(n, m, k, rep) {
  document.getElementById('sel-n').value = n;
  document.getElementById('sel-m').value = m;
  document.getElementById('sel-k').value = k;
  document.getElementById('sel-rep').value = rep;
  window.updateSelectionDims();
};

// WIDGET 5: §2.4.3 Dynamical Phase Trichotomy SVG Plotter
window.updateTrichotomy = function() {
  const elN0 = document.getElementById('tri-n0');
  if (!elN0) return;
  let n0 = parseInt(elN0.value);
  let m = parseInt(document.getElementById('tri-m').value);
  document.getElementById('tri-n0-val').innerText = n0;
  document.getElementById('tri-m-val').innerText = m;

  let seq = [n0];
  let curr = n0;
  for (let g = 1; g <= 5; g++) {
    if (curr > 10000) {
      seq.push("1.11×10¹⁴");
      break;
    }
    curr = window.comb2(curr, m);
    seq.push(curr);
  }

  let regime = "", col = "#FFD700";
  if (n0 <= m) {
    regime = "SUB-CRITICAL EXTINCTION (n₀ ≤ m ⇒ Syndromabschluß at γ ≤ 2)";
    col = "#ff6b81";
  } else if (n0 === m + 1) {
    regime = "CRITICAL EQUI-SYNDROMATIC FIXED POINT (n₀ = m + 1 ⇒ Constant n_γ = " + n0 + ")";
    col = "#20B2AA";
  } else {
    regime = "SUPER-CRITICAL DOUBLY-EXPONENTIAL REGIME (n₀ ≥ m + 2 ⇒ Rapid Explosion)";
    col = "#FFA500";
  }

  // Update SVG Plot
  const poly = document.getElementById('tri-poly');
  const dotsGrp = document.getElementById('tri-dots');
  if (poly && dotsGrp) {
    let pts = [];
    let dotsHtml = "";
    let numSteps = Math.min(4, seq.length);
    for (let i = 0; i < numSteps; i++) {
      let val = typeof seq[i] === 'number' ? seq[i] : 500;
      let logY = val <= 0 ? 0 : Math.min(1.0, Math.log10(val + 1) / 3.8);
      let x = 30 + i * 52;
      let y = (92 - logY * 74).toFixed(1);
      pts.push(`${x},${y}`);
      dotsHtml += `<circle cx="${x}" cy="${y}" r="4.5" fill="${col}"/>`;
    }
    poly.setAttribute('points', pts.join(' '));
    poly.setAttribute('stroke', col);
    dotsGrp.innerHTML = dotsHtml;
  }

  const box = document.getElementById('tri-trajectory');
  if (box) {
    box.style.borderLeftColor = col;
    box.style.color = col;
    box.innerHTML = `<b>${regime}</b><br>Trajectory (γ = 0 … 5): ` + seq.join("  →  ");
  }
};

window.setTriPreset = function(n0, m) {
  document.getElementById('tri-n0').value = n0;
  document.getElementById('tri-m').value = m;
  window.updateTrichotomy();
};

// WIDGET 6: §2.5 Beck Coherence Tab Switcher
window.showBeckTab = function(idx, btnEl) {
  for (let i = 1; i <= 4; i++) {
    const p = document.getElementById('beck-pane-' + i);
    if (p) p.classList.toggle('active', i === idx);
  }
  if (btnEl && btnEl.parentElement) {
    Array.from(btnEl.parentElement.children).forEach(b => b.classList.remove('active'));
    btnEl.classList.add('active');
  }
  if (window.MathJax && window.MathJax.typesetPromise) {
    window.MathJax.typesetPromise().catch(() => {});
  }
};

// WIDGET 7: §2.6–2.7 Stability & Spine Reflexivity Tab Switcher
window.showStabTab = function(idx, btnEl) {
  for (let i = 1; i <= 4; i++) {
    const p = document.getElementById('stab-pane-' + i);
    if (p) p.classList.toggle('active', i === idx);
  }
  if (btnEl && btnEl.parentElement) {
    Array.from(btnEl.parentElement.children).forEach(b => b.classList.remove('active'));
    btnEl.classList.add('active');
  }
  if (window.MathJax && window.MathJax.typesetPromise) {
    window.MathJax.typesetPromise().catch(() => {});
  }
};

// WIDGET 8: §2.8 Polycyclic Metrophorischer Zirkel & Holonomy Lab
window.updateMetrophoricCircle = function() {
  const elZ = document.getElementById('cir-z');
  if (!elZ) return;
  let Z = parseInt(elZ.value);
  let N = parseInt(document.getElementById('cir-n').value);
  let phi = parseFloat(document.getElementById('cir-phi').value);

  document.getElementById('cir-z-val').innerText = Z;
  document.getElementById('cir-n-val').innerText = N;
  document.getElementById('cir-phi-val').innerText = phi.toFixed(0) + '°';

  let L = window.comb2(Z, 2);
  let degTruth = L * N;

  const svg = document.getElementById('cir-svg');
  if (svg) {
    let html = `<circle cx="0" cy="0" r="52" fill="none" stroke="#334155" stroke-dasharray="3,2"/>`;
    let pts = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < Z; i++) {
      let a = (i / Z) * 2 * Math.PI - Math.PI / 2;
      pts.push({ x: 52 * Math.cos(a), y: 52 * Math.sin(a) });
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < Z; i++) {
      for (let j = i + 1; j < Z; j++) {
        html += `<line x1="${pts[i].x.toFixed(1)}" y1="${pts[i].y.toFixed(1)}" x2="${pts[j].x.toFixed(1)}" y2="${pts[j].y.toFixed(1)}" stroke="rgba(65,105,225,0.45)" stroke-width="1.3"/>`;
      }
    }
    pts.forEach((p, idx) => {
      html += `<circle cx="${p.x.toFixed(1)}" cy="${p.y.toFixed(1)}" r="7" fill="#20B2AA" stroke="#fff" stroke-width="1"/>`;
    });
    let rad = (phi - 90) * Math.PI / 180.0;
    let hx = (52 * Math.cos(rad)).toFixed(1), hy = (52 * Math.sin(rad)).toFixed(1);
    html += `<circle cx="${hx}" cy="${hy}" r="6" fill="#FFD700" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5"/>`;
    svg.innerHTML = html;
  }

  const box = document.getElementById('cir-readout');
  if (box) {
    box.innerText =
      `Z = ${Z} Aspect Systems ⇒ Partial Circles L = C(${Z}, 2) = ${L}  |  Bounded Universalquantor Degree ∑ N_j = ${degTruth} (Thm 2.22(5))`;
  }
};

function ensureVideosPlaying() {
  document.querySelectorAll('video').forEach(v => {
    v.muted = true;
    v.playsInline = true;
    if (v.paused) v.play().catch(() => {});
  });
}

function initAllCh2Widgets() {
  window.updateBandsyntrix();
  window.setOperadTreeMode('two');
  window.updateSelectionDims();
  window.updateTrichotomy();
  window.updateMetrophoricCircle();
  ensureVideosPlaying();

  document.querySelectorAll('input[type="range"], select, button').forEach(input => {
    input.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
    input.addEventListener('mousedown', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
    input.addEventListener('touchstart', (e) => e.stopPropagation(), {passive: true});
  });

  if ('IntersectionObserver' in window) {
    const obs = new IntersectionObserver((entries) => {
      entries.forEach(entry => {
        if (entry.isIntersecting && entry.target.tagName === 'VIDEO') {
          entry.target.muted = true;
          entry.target.play().catch(() => {});
        }
      });
    }, { threshold: 0.15 });
    document.querySelectorAll('video').forEach(v => obs.observe(v));
  }
}

if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
  document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", initAllCh2Widgets);
} else {
  initAllCh2Widgets();
}

window.addEventListener('load', initAllCh2Widgets);
if (window.Reveal) {
  window.Reveal.on('ready', initAllCh2Widgets);
  window.Reveal.on('slidechanged', initAllCh2Widgets);
}
</script>
